rationale: The literature demonstrates that SNUPN-related disorders represent a continuous phenotypic and allelic continuum rather than mutually exclusive variant categories. Pathogenic variants in SNUPN disrupt snurportin-1-mediated nuclear import of U1 snRNPs across tissues, but manifestations vary from isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMDR29) to complex neurodevelopmental phenotypes and spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA). Okubo et al. showed that SNUPN variants impair U1 snRNP nuclear transport and global splicing in Purkinje cells (disrupting dendritic arborization, synaptic organization, and sonic hedgehog secretion), yet human patients with these variants showed discordant muscle involvement (one with mild skeletal muscle alterations and another with none). Furthermore, Muelas et al. identified adult-onset siblings carrying identical compound heterozygous SNUPN variants where one presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy while the other did not. These findings demonstrate that cell-type-specific vulnerability to spliceosomal trafficking failure, rather than strict variant-level segregation, governs the clinical ratio of cerebellar versus skeletal muscle pathology.

evidence.text: Okubo et al. identified biallelic SNUPN variants in two families with spinocerebellar atrophy. Patient-derived variants disrupted snurportin-1 binding to importin-beta and nuclear import of U1 snRNPs, causing aberrant splicing and downregulation of developmental and synaptic genes in Purkinje cells, abnormal dendritic development, and reduced sonic hedgehog secretion in knock-in mice. In human subjects, skeletal muscle involvement was dissociated: one patient had mild changes while the other had none.

source.title: SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy by disrupting global splicing in cerebellar Purkinje cells
source.quote: Mutations in the SNUPN gene, which encodes snurportin-1, a nuclear import adaptor for U1 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNP), have recently been implicated in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, attributed to disrupted pre-messenger RNA splicing in skeletal muscle... One patient exhibited mild changes in skeletal muscle, while the other did not... Abnormal RNA splicing and reduced expression were observed in many genes related to neuronal development and synaptic organization in Purkinje cells, leading to an immature cytoskeleton and reduced secretion of sonic hedgehog.

evidence.text: Muelas et al. reported that SNUPN-related disease encompasses a continuum ranging from pure childhood- or adult-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy to complex phenotypes with neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia. They identified two siblings with adult-onset proximo-distal and axial weakness where one harbored asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy, demonstrating intrafamilial variability in cerebellar manifestation.

source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia... Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement. One patient presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: Iruzubieta et al. delineated the core muscular phenotype of LGMDR29 across five patients from two families carrying the homozygous p.Ile309Ser SNUPN variant, establishing prominent early contractures, childhood-onset proximal weakness, and early restrictive respiratory failure alongside myofibrillar pathology and selective MRI involvement of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, and calf muscles, without primary ataxia.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: Here, we present five patients from two unrelated families with a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD) phenotype carrying a biallelic variant in SNUPN gene... SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures, although inter-individual variability in terms of severity even in individuals from the same family was found.

evidence.text: Nashabat et al. identified 18 pediatric patients across 15 families harboring 9 biallelic hypomorphic SNUPN variants clustered in the terminal coding exon, exhibiting atypical muscular dystrophy combined with central nervous system and neurological defects driven by sarcolemmal mis-splicing and spliceosomal disruption.

source.title: SNUPN deficiency causes a recessive muscular dystrophy due to RNA mis-splicing and ECM dysregulation
source.quote: In this study, we investigate 18 children from 15 unrelated families who present with atypical muscular dystrophy and neurological defects. Nine hypomorphic SNUPN biallelic variants, predominantly clustered in the last coding exon, are ascertained to segregate with the disease.

new_directions.question_text: What specific pre-mRNA splice targets in human Purkinje cells versus human skeletal myotubes are most sensitive to partial nuclear U1 snRNP depletion?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative RNA-seq of human iPSC-derived Purkinje neurons and myotubes under graded SNUPN hypomorphism will reveal whether alternative splicing thresholds differ cell-autonomously between cerebellar and muscular transcripts.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of patients diagnosed with unexplained recessive spinocerebellar ataxia exhibit subclinical dystrophic or myofibrillar changes on muscle MRI or biopsy?
new_directions.rationale: Given that cerebellar atrophy can overshadow mild myopathy in SNUPN variants, systematic skeletal muscle imaging in SCA cohorts will determine the frequency of occult LGMDR29-pattern myopathy.
